key_insight: Reasoning graphs capture deeper authorship signals than surface text features, making LLM-generated text attribution more robust to obfuscation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical detection pipeline for deployed systems that must identify LLM-authored content even when text is paraphrased, backtranslated, or produced by new model versions.
method: Extract reasoning structures from text using an argument mining pipeline.
Represent these structures as graphs and classify them with a graph neural network.
Compare against a Longformer baseline focused on surface-level features.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gains of up to 27 percentage points under paraphrasing/backtranslation attacks and 19 percentage points on texts from unseen LLM versions.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the argument mining step, which could introduce errors or brittleness in noisy or low-resource settings.
paper_title: Show Me How You Reason and I'll Tell You Who You Are: Reasoning Graphs for Robust LLM Authorship Attribution
